# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Ranking: your partner's words, 2026-11-10 ("Rank them in the order you listed"). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly baseline
      Objective: Download a small configured range of real archived quarterly master indexes with an identified client throttled to 3 req/s, keep the original bytes locally, and parse them into canonical rows in Parquet.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (generated package scaffolds only)
      Produces: the shared downloader and parser; local raw snapshots with their SHA-256; canonical `sec-index-v1` rows in Parquet; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — a real run over the configured range keeps every quarter's original bytes and SHA-256 on local disk. O3 — the same run writes canonical rows (§4.5 row contract) per quarter, and their row counts match the source data lines. Measured cost of the real run, per quarter: requests, achieved request rate, bytes, rows, elapsed time and peak memory.
      Leaves out: daily indexes (Stage 2); the shared lease and config validation (Stage 3); provenance fields, processing states, overlap deduplication, generations, manifests and the pointer (Stage 4); reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 5); Azure services (Stage 6); legacy-format golden fixtures for the full range, scheduling, alerts and runbooks (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries, through the same commands as backfill.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, parser and canonical Parquet output (Stage 1 findings)
      Produces: daily discovery state and its boundary; one `discover`/`collect`/`transform` command set that serves both quarterly and daily sources
      Exit: O2 — a real run from a handoff date ingests every listed daily index and reports `no_new_sources` on a valid empty listing; fixture runs covering a missed run, an outage across quarters and a failed listing keep pending sources discoverable and do not advance the boundary. O5 — backfill and daily runs go through one downloader, one parser and one writer.
      Leaves out: shared lease budget (Stage 3); overlap deduplication and precedence (Stage 4); Azure scheduling (Stages 6–7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Shared request budget and validated settings
      Objective: Route every SEC request through one collector lease and request budget, and validate configuration before any I/O.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 2's backfill and daily collectors
      Produces: a single lease-governed request budget that all SEC access passes through; typed configuration with the §4.8 keys
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily runs, retries included, stay within the configured rate in aggregate, and lease loss or takeover never produces two concurrent request issuers (§6 Access). O11 — invalid configuration (missing User-Agent, a rate at or above 10 req/s, a reversed range, a second collector) is refused before any network request.
      Leaves out: the Storage-backed lease on Azure (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Replay and versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Keep source, snapshot and processing identities, rebuild from stored raw bytes, and publish complete quarter generations behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 1 raw snapshots; Stage 2 daily and quarterly observations; Stage 3 configuration, including parser and schema versions
      Produces: §4.5 manifest records and observation output; §4.4 identity, overlap deduplication and open-quarter precedence; per-quarter generations with `manifest.json`, `changes.parquet` and an active pointer, backed locally
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds the catalog from stored raw bytes with SEC access disabled, with no duplicate logical records and no work done for unchanged hashes. O9 — readers resolve each quarter through the pointer to an explicit file list; crashes injected before files finish, before the pointer update and after it leave only complete generations readable, and competing publishers lose no update (§6 Publication).
      Leaves out: closed-quarter withdrawals and reconciliation (Stage 5); Table Storage conditional writes and ADLS paths (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and hold any key removal for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4 generations, pointer, manifest and change reports; Stage 3 shared budget
      Produces: the reconciliation workflow; withdrawal approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — a reconciliation run over the backfilled quarters skips unchanged hashes and publishes additions and field updates with their change report. O10 — open-quarter absence withdraws nothing; a closed-quarter replacement that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its exact hash and candidate; stale daily replay cannot bring back a withdrawn key (§6 Reconciliation).
      Leaves out: scheduled weekly runs (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure deployment in an isolated environment
      Objective: Run the shared image on the ADR's Azure services in an isolated environment, with production triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 commands as one image; Stage 3 lease and Stage 4 pointer contracts
      Produces: versioned infrastructure (§4.9); ADF pipelines and Container Apps Jobs; ADLS and Table Storage backing for §4.5; managed identities; log delivery
      Exit: O4 — ADF starts and polls backfill, daily and reconciliation jobs to a terminal outcome; §6 integration tests and the orchestration criteria pass; a bounded live smoke test of one archived quarter and one daily index records the §7 step 4 figures, and replay with SEC access disabled gives unchanged output (§7 steps 3–5); the environment's Azure cost is measured.
      Leaves out: production triggers, alerts and runbooks (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and daily catch-up, then enable the scheduled runs with monitoring and runbooks exercised.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O4, O7
      Consumes: Stage 6 environment, image and smoke-test record
      Produces: an active production catalog; a release record; enabled triggers
      Exit: O1 — golden fixtures cover every historical format in the chosen range (§4.6), and every requested baseline unit is published or an approved incomplete range is recorded. O2 — catch-up from the handoff date is accepted, the daily trigger is enabled, and the next scheduled runs match their durable reports. O4 — the §4.7 alerts and the §8 runbooks are exercised, and the release record names the image, the configuration and the active generations. O7 — one manual reconciliation runs, its gated candidates are resolved, and the weekly trigger is enabled.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
